Account.description:
Someone with their email, as they see themself and as the organisers
of a contest they registered for see them.
Account.title: Account

Announcement.description:
One announcement: where it is, by the names of its contest and task,
its number there, what it says, when it was posted, whether it is
closed, whether it answers a question, and, for an organiser, which.
Announcement.title: Announcement

AnnouncementRequest.description: An announcement's title and text, as posted or as edited.
AnnouncementRequest.title: AnnouncementRequest

AnsweredQuestion.description:
The clarification an announcement answers: whose desk it is in, the
asker's user id or `team.<id>` for a team's, and the question's number
there.
AnsweredQuestion.title: AnsweredQuestion

Board.description:
One board as the reader sees it now. `nothing_shown` is true, with no
rows, while its scope shows nothing yet; `shown_at` is then the time its
first group is shown, null while no task it covers is released.
Board.title: Board

BoardCell.description:
A row's cell on a task: whether it counts, its number on each key it
has one for, by the key's `by`, while it counts, and its attempts.
`grading`, how many of the row's submissions are not graded yet, and
`submissions`, the numbers of those it counts, several under
`best_per_group`, come only in the reader's own row, and are null in
every other.
BoardCell.title: BoardCell

BoardKey.description:
One key rows are ranked on, in turn: what it ranks by, `points`,
`penalty` or a declared value, which way is better, null for a value no
covered task gives a direction, and, on `penalty`, the minutes each
attempt before the counted submission charges; a `per_attempt` of 0
charges nothing, so the minute submitted is all it ranks on.
BoardKey.title: BoardKey

BoardRow.description:
A row on the board: its rank, shared by rows tied on every key, whose
it is, its number on each of the board's keys in turn, null where it
has none, and its cell on each task by the task's name.
BoardRow.title: BoardRow

BoardRowOwner.description:
Whose a row is: a contestant by `user_id`, or a team by its id as
`team`, and its name, a team's own or a contestant's username, empty
when the forge gives none.
BoardRowOwner.title: BoardRowOwner

BoardTask.description:
A task the board covers: its name as `id`, its `label`, the letter of
its place in the contest, and its `worth`, null on a task that gives no
points.
BoardTask.title: BoardTask

CallbackAnswer.description: Where the grading stands once its run's report is taken.
CallbackAnswer.title: CallbackAnswer

CancelRequest.description: Why staff end the submission, a sentence its contestant reads.
CancelRequest.title: CancelRequest

Change.description:
One entry of a place's history: the version it made, who made it, what
they said about it and when.
Change.title: Change

CheckDefinition.description: A `workflow.yaml` to check as a version would be, writing nothing.
CheckDefinition.title: CheckDefinition

Checked.description:
Every problem a version would be refused for; none means it would be
made.
Checked.title: Checked

Clarification.description:
One question: its contest by name, whose desk it is in, the asker's
user id or `team.<id>` for a team's, its number there, the task it
names, what it asks, when, whether it is answered and whether it is
open, and every message under it, oldest first.
Clarification.title: Clarification

Closed.description:
Why a task is not open to a row, the first of these that applies; and,
to a person who holds no approved row, `not_approved` where it is
otherwise open, as a submit would be refused.
Closed.title: Closed

CombineWorkflows.description:
A workflow to make as `name` under `owner` from two or more
`sources`, each `<owner>/<name>@<version>`, inlined in their order.
CombineWorkflows.title: CombineWorkflows

CommentRequest.description:
One message under a question: a contestant's follow-up or an
organiser's reply.
CommentRequest.title: CommentRequest

ContestHome.description:
A contest's home for the caller. `organises` says the caller holds a
role at the contest, which keeps them from registering;
`registration_open` says whether the registration window is open now,
`invite_only` whether only invited people may register and `asks_code`
whether registering takes the contest's code.
ContestHome.title: ContestHome

ContestNames.description: A contest by the names of its org and itself.
ContestNames.title: ContestNames

ContestSummary.description:
A contest the caller sees, with its title, when it runs, who sees it,
and the caller's own registration status.
ContestSummary.title: ContestSummary

ContestVisibility.description:
Who sees the contest at all: anyone, guests included; anyone signed
in; or only its contestants and organisers.
ContestVisibility.title: ContestVisibility

Contestant.description:
One registration as the contest's organisers read it: the same
fields, and who the person is, null once their account is gone.
Contestant.title: Contestant

CopyWorkflow.description:
A copy to make of `source`, `<owner>/<name>@<version>`, as `name`
under `owner`, which follows the rule for making one.
CopyWorkflow.title: CopyWorkflow

CreateContest.description: A contest to make, titled `title` or, without one, its name.
CreateContest.title: CreateContest

CreateTask.description: A task to make, titled `title` or, without one, its name.
CreateTask.title: CreateTask

CreateVersion.description:
A name to freeze the saved draft under, such as `v1`, and the token
the caller saved it with, so the version is of that save; with none, of
whatever is saved now.
CreateVersion.title: CreateVersion

CreateWorkflow.description:
A workflow to make under `owner`: the caller's own username, or the
name of an org where they hold the manager role or above.
CreateWorkflow.title: CreateWorkflow

DeclaredField.description:
One field every test of the workflow has: its name, its type and its
options on an enum.
DeclaredField.title: DeclaredField

DeclaredInput.description:
One input a workflow declares, as the task form shows it: its id, its
type, whether the contestant gives it, its options on an enum, whether
it is given once per test, and whether a task may leave it out. A
workflow gives no defaults: a contestant input's `default` is the
task's, in `task.yaml`.
DeclaredInput.title: DeclaredInput

Definition.description:
A `workflow.yaml` as text, and the token a save of it carries back:
none for one that is not there yet.
Definition.title: Definition

DefinitionError.description:
One thing wrong with a definition file: its YAML path, "" for the file
as a whole, and a sentence a form shows beside that field.
DefinitionError.title: DefinitionError

DefinitionProblem.description:
One problem: its YAML path in `workflow.yaml`, `steps[1].with.binary`,
and what is wrong there. The path is empty for the file as a whole.
DefinitionProblem.title: DefinitionProblem

Draft.description:
A save kept as a draft: the version its files were written as, the
errors that kept it from publishing, and what it held back.
Draft.title: Draft

ExtensionRequest.description:
How long, in seconds, the extension moves the due and the close of
each of the contest's `tasks`, by name, or of every task when it names
none, in place of any extension there was.
ExtensionRequest.title: ExtensionRequest

Fallback.description:
Why a submission counts as its last good result in place of its
latest attempt, a system error or staff cancelled: staff asked so on
that attempt, or the contest's `on_system_error` says so.
Fallback.title: Fallback

FeedEntry.description:
One grading among a task's or a contest's: the grading as an
organiser reads it, its task by name, null for a task the platform has
no name for, its `label`, the letter of its place in the contest's
`tasks`, null once the contest no longer lists it or its settings do
not read, and `by`, who made the submission: a contestant by `user_id`
and username as `name`, or a team by its id as `team` and its `name`,
the name null once the account or the team is gone.
FeedEntry.title: FeedEntry

FileChange.description:
One file of a save, typed or uploaded for this path, with the token it
was read with, or null for a file the save creates.
FileChange.title: FileChange

FileContent.description:
One file at one version, with the token a write presents back, and
`upload` when it is a file an organiser uploaded: its `content` is then
the pointer to the bytes, never opened as text, and `upload` the size
and SHA-256 of what it holds. A typed file has none.
FileContent.title: FileContent

ForgeUrl.description:
Where a browser reaches the forge's own pages: sign-in and the account
settings. No trailing slash.
ForgeUrl.title: ForgeUrl

GradedTest.description:
One test's row of a result: its id, `<group>/<test>`, its outcome,
and the values its steps reported for it. Scored, it carries its credit,
from 0 to 1, and, on a relative credit, the best value that credit is
measured against; both are null otherwise.
GradedTest.title: GradedTest

Grading.description:
One grading as an organiser managing its task reads it: the
submission by its number, the publication it grades against, its
attempt and whether that is the submission's `latest`, the one staff
cancel or retry, where it stands, the reason it failed, the sentence
staff cancelled it with, its result, whether its log was written, the
last progress its run reported, and its times.

On a latest attempt that is a system error or staff cancelled,
`last_good` is the latest earlier attempt that finished with a result,
and `fallback` why its submission counts as that attempt now: `staff`,
who asked so on this one, or `contest`, whose `on_system_error` is
`last_result`; null while it counts as still grading, or void once
cancelled. `falls_back` is staff having asked so on this one.
Grading.title: Grading

GradingProgress.description:
The last progress a grading's run reported: the step it was at and how
many of that step's containers were done of how many.
GradingProgress.title: GradingProgress

GradingStatus.description:
Where one grading stands. `queued` waits for its run to be started,
which happens as soon as the request that made it commits; `dispatched`
is held by the CI, waiting for a machine or checking out; `running` has
had its envelope fetched by the harness. It ends `done` with a result,
`system_error`, a grading that failed for a reason of the platform's,
never a grade: its run could not be started, or did not report before
its deadline; or `cancelled`, by staff ending one in `system_error`, or
by a rejudge replacing one still being graded.
GradingStatus.title: GradingStatus

Grant.description:
What an invite gives once accepted: a contestant's place in a contest,
which is eligibility to register for it, or one of the organiser roles
at the invite's scope.
Grant.title: Grant

GrantRequest.description:
Give the named user `role` at the scope, moving them from any other
role they hold directly there.
GrantRequest.title: GrantRequest

GroupShown.description:
One test group as the contestant sees it now: its name, its `show`,
its outcome once its verdict is shown, its tests once they are, when
what is held back is shown, null once nothing is, and whether it ran on
this grading. A group that did not run has no outcome, no tests and
nothing held back. On a task that gives points, `max` is the most the
group gives and `points` what it gave, once its verdict is shown.
GroupShown.title: GroupShown

HeldRole.description: A role the user holds, at the org, contest or task `names` reaches.
HeldRole.title: HeldRole

Holder.description:
Someone holding `role` at the scope asked about, held directly at
`at_names`: that scope, or a broader one, such as the org of a contest
whose admin is listed at the contest.
Holder.title: Holder

InputField.description:
One input the contestant gives, with what its form shows: its
`type`, its `label`, the `options` of an enum, whether it takes one file
per test, `per_test`, named for the test as `<group>/<test>`, the
`default` a value takes when it is left out, `min` and `max` of a
number, exactly, and `max_size`, the most its files may total in bytes. The
submit panel shows one field or drop zone per input.
InputField.title: InputField

Invite.description:
An invite: where it is to, by its names, what it grants, the username
or the address it names, who sent it, where it stands, whether it has
lapsed, its dates, and what became of its mail: `waiting`, `sent`,
`failed`, or `off` where the deployment sends no mail.
Invite.title: Invite

InviteRequest.description:
Who to invite, by exactly one of `username` and `email`, to what, and
for how many days the invite stands, 14 unless given.
InviteRequest.title: InviteRequest

InviteToTeamRequest.description: The username of the approved contestant the leader asks in.
InviteToTeamRequest.title: InviteToTeamRequest

LimitSource.description:
A container limit raised to `input * scale + add` when that is more,
`scale` and `add` exactly as the declaration writes them.
LimitSource.title: LimitSource

ListedTeam.description:
A team as a contestant choosing one sees it: its name, its leader, and
how many are in it of how many the contest allows.
ListedTeam.title: ListedTeam

MailStatus.description:
What became of an invite's mail: `waiting` until it is handed to the
mail server, `sent` once it took it, `failed` when it could not be sent,
the server refusing, not answering, or there being no address to send it
to, and `off` where the deployment has no mail server. A mail still
`waiting` minutes on was cut short by a restart, and is sent again from
the invite.
MailStatus.title: MailStatus

Marks.description:
The marks the caller's row holds on a task for its `marked` boards:
the numbers of the submissions marked, the most it may hold, and the
row's close on the task, after which they are frozen.
Marks.title: Marks

Me.description:
The signed-in user and their roles at every scope. `degraded` is set
when the forge did not answer and the identity comes from the session.
Me.title: Me

Member.description:
Someone in a team, or asking or asked to be: their id, who they are,
or none once their account is gone, where they stand, and since when.
Member.title: Member

Message.description:
One message under a question: whether the asker wrote it, what it
says, and when.
Message.title: Message

MyRegistration.description:
The caller's own registration: where it stands, when it was made and
last decided, why it was rejected, and their own extension: how long, in
seconds, it moves the due and the close of the tasks in
`extension_tasks`, or of every task when that is null. It holds while
they work alone; in a team, the team's holds.
MyRegistration.title: MyRegistration

MyTeams.description:
The caller's team in the contest, if any, the teams they are asked
into or have asked to join, and how many a team holds.
MyTeams.title: MyTeams

Named.description: An org, a contest or a task, by the name people call it.
Named.title: Named

NotInView.description:
What of a task is in the board's scope and not in its numbers yet:
the groups whose verdict is not shown, and, on a board ranking a value,
the `verdict` groups whose tests are not shown, with when they join.
NotInView.title: NotInView

NotReady.description:
Deliberately not a problem document: an orchestrator reads the status in
a fixed place. What failed underneath is in the log and not here.
NotReady.title: NotReady

OpenInviteRequest.description: The token after the `#` of the link an invite's mail carried.
OpenInviteRequest.title: OpenInviteRequest

OrgProfile.description:
An org's own fields at the forge, which its admin changes: the name it
is shown under, none while it has none of its own, and its description.
OrgProfile.title: OrgProfile

OrganiseTeamRequest.description:
A new team's name, and the username of the approved contestant who
leads it, or none for an empty team.
OrganiseTeamRequest.title: OrganiseTeamRequest

OrganisedBoard.description:
A board as organisers read it: `now`, every row given, or as the row
picked sees it; `final`, every group of its scope counted as after the
reveal; and what it asks of the tasks it covers that does not hold, each
a sentence, which the save reported when the tasks were published.
OrganisedBoard.title: OrganisedBoard

Over.description: Which test groups a board counts, by each group's declared `show`.
Over.title: Over

Person.description:
Someone as another person sees them, by their forge id. Their email
stays out.
Person.title: Person

Points.description:
A submission's points as its contestant sees them: those shown, those
still pending on groups whose verdict is not shown yet, and when they
are shown, null when none are pending.
Points.title: Points

Primitive.description:
One version of a primitive, `ref` being what a step's `use:` names.
Its declaration is in `batch`, `network`, `limits`, `limits_from`,
`inputs` and `outputs`; a version in a format the platform no longer
reads has none of them and `problem` instead, so no step uses it.
Primitive.title: Primitive

PrimitivePort.description:
One port: its type, the options an enum takes, whether it may be left
out, and on an input whether the primitive runs what arrives there and
whether it keeps it from the program it runs.
PrimitivePort.title: PrimitivePort

Problem.description: Extra members are allowed: `sole_admin` carries `scopes`, for instance.
Problem.title: Problem

PublicContest.description:
A public contest `where` it is, by the names of its org and itself,
with its title as `name`, what it says of itself and when it runs.
`tasks` are its released tasks, and empty in the list of contests.
PublicContest.title: PublicContest

PublicStatement.description: A released task of a public contest with its statement in Markdown.
PublicStatement.title: PublicStatement

PublicTask.description:
A released task of a public contest: its name, the label the contest
gives it, and its title.
PublicTask.title: PublicTask

Publication.description:
One publication: its number among the task's publications, the version
it froze, whether it changed how the task grades and what, and when.
Which workflow each of its workflow names was at the forge stays out.
Publication.title: Publication

Published.description:
A save that published: the new publication's number among the task's,
whether it changed how the task grades, and what, the notes the save
makes of the task beside publishing it, such as which steps it seals
until the reveal, and how many submissions it `regraded`, queued to be
graded again against it.
Published.title: Published

QuestionRequest.description:
A question's title and text, and the name of the task it is about,
when it is about one released to the asker.
QuestionRequest.title: QuestionRequest

QueueDepth.description:
How many of a contest's gradings wait for a machine: `queued`, whose
run is not started yet, and `dispatched`, whose run the CI holds until a
machine takes it.
QueueDepth.title: QueueDepth

Rate.description: At most `count` submissions in any `per` seconds.
Rate.title: Rate

Reader.description: Someone a workflow is shared with, by their username.
Reader.title: Reader

RegisterRequest.description: The code the contest asks for, when it asks for one.
RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest

RejectRequest.description: Why, in words the person reads on their own page.
RejectRequest.title: RejectRequest

Rejudged.description:
What a rejudge did: the publication the new attempts grade against,
how many it queued, how many unfinished attempts against an older
publication it cancelled first, and how many it left to finish against
the current one.
Rejudged.title: Rejudged

Reported.description:
The values a run reported, by name: its numbers, exactly, and its
texts, each of at most 10,000 characters.
Reported.title: Reported

Result.description:
The latest attempt of a submission's grading, as its contestant sees
it: its id, attempt and status, and once it is done, what stopped the
run, the outcome over the groups shown, each test group as its `show`
allows, the values reported once, and `folded`, each per-test value
with a fold, folded over the tests shown, a test without it counting as
its worst bound. A run that failed on the platform's side is `running`
to its contestant, with nothing else, until staff end it: then it is
`cancelled`, with `reason`, the sentence they gave, which is null on
every other status. Once done on a task that gives points, it carries
its `points` and the late `factor` they include; both are null
otherwise. While a sealed step's stop is held to the reveal, nothing of
the run is shown: every group reads as hidden.
Result.title: Result

RollbackFile.description:
Write the file as it was at `version` back as a new change, `token`
being the one of the file as it is now.
RollbackFile.title: RollbackFile

RunResult.description:
What a run's result says of the submission: what stopped the run,
null when nothing did, a row for every test, the values reported once,
and, when it stopped on `system_error`, the sentence for staff saying
why. Where the run put its log stays out.
RunResult.title: RunResult

SaveDefinition.description:
A draft to write over the one read with `token`, or to create when
the token is none. Whatever it holds saves, problems and all.
SaveDefinition.title: SaveDefinition

SaveRequest.description:
The files a save writes, several at once. `keep_as_draft` writes them
as a draft that says what it held back and publishes nothing, on any
save. Otherwise, while the task's contest runs, `confirm` publishes a
change to how the task grades; an empty save with `confirm` publishes a
draft kept earlier.
SaveRequest.title: SaveRequest

ScopeNames.description:
The names of the org, the contest and the task a scope reaches, as far
down as it does, in the shape of an address: `acme`, `acme/spring`,
`acme/spring/sum`.
ScopeNames.title: ScopeNames

Select.description: Which of a row's submissions to a task a board counts.
Select.title: Select

SessionInfo.description:
One place this user is signed in, described by its device and its
times. The address a session came from is kept for the record and stays
out of the answer.
SessionInfo.title: SessionInfo

SetVisibility.description:
Private, shared or public. Private and public empty the list of
readers; shared keeps it.
SetVisibility.title: SetVisibility

Show.description:
When contestants see a test group's results: as soon as a grading
ends; its outcome and points now and its tests at the task's reveal; or
everything but its name and its most points at the reveal.
Show.title: Show

Slot.description:
A slot for one file: where to send it, and when the slot stops being
good. `ready` is true for a file the forge already holds, which is sent
again by sending nothing.
Slot.title: Slot

Submission.description:
One of the caller's submissions of the task: its number among them,
when it was taken, how many started days after their due it was, and
its grading.
Submission.title: Submission

Submissions.description:
What a submit is counted against: at most `max` submissions in all,
and at most `rate` of them in any window.
Submissions.title: Submissions

SubmitRequest.description:
A submit: `idempotency_key` is 8 to 128 letters, digits, `-` and `_`,
made once by the browser for this submit, so sending it again answers
with the submission it made and makes nothing. `inputs` is keyed by the
id of each of the task's contestant inputs, and forge checks them
against the task's inputs; a value left out takes its default.
SubmitRequest.title: SubmitRequest

SubmittedFileInput.description:
What one input of a submission was: the paths of its files in the
submission, each a download through the download door, or the value
given. It is read leniently from the submission's `submission.json`: a
member of the wrong type is left out rather than failing the answer.
SubmittedFileInput.title: SubmittedFileInput

SubmittedFiles.description: What a submission was made with, by input id.
SubmittedFiles.title: SubmittedFiles

SubmittedInput.description:
What a contestant gives for one input: the uploads of its files; or,
for a text, number, true-or-false or enum input, its value.
SubmittedInput.title: SubmittedInput

Submitter.description:
Who made a submission, as an organiser recognises them: a contestant,
by user id and username, or a team, by id and name. The name is none
once the account or the team is gone, or when the forge did not say.
Submitter.title: Submitter

TaskEntry.description:
A task released to the caller: its name, the label its place in the
contest gives it, its title, the most points it gives, null on a task
that gives none, whether they may submit to it now, and when it falls
due, null when it has no due, and closes for them, their extension on it
included.
TaskEntry.title: TaskEntry

TaskFileUploadRequest.description:
One file an organiser puts into the task: the `path` it goes to in the
task's files, its size in bytes, the SHA-256 of its content in lowercase
hex and, when the browser knows it, its content type.
TaskFileUploadRequest.title: TaskFileUploadRequest

TaskPage.description:
A task as the caller reads it: its statement in Markdown, the caps a
submit is counted against, the inputs a contestant gives, when it falls
due and closes for them, and `marks`, how many of their row's
submissions they may mark for the `marked` boards, null unless such a
board covers the task and they are an approved contestant; and nothing
else the task holds.
TaskPage.title: TaskPage

TaskRelease.description:
Whether the task is released, visible and open to one person now, and
when it is not open, the first reason why.
TaskRelease.title: TaskRelease

TaskStanding.description:
One task of a contest as its organisers work from it: the task by
name, its letter by its place in the contest's `tasks`, where its files
stand as `GET <task>` gives it, and its timeline from its entry, each
time at its default where the entry gives none: `worth`, null on a task
that gives no points or has no publication, `release_at`, `due` and
`late_per_day`, both null on a task with no due, and `closes`.
TaskStanding.title: TaskStanding

TaskState.description:
Where a task's files stand: the version at their head, the latest
publication or none, and whether the head is a draft, a state no
publication froze. A draft carries the errors that keep it from
publishing; a draft with none was held back, or has not been saved since
it was made.
TaskState.title: TaskState

Team.description:
A team: its name, its leader's user id, its members, the people
asking or asked in, whether it has submitted anything, and its
extension: how long, in seconds, it moves the due and the close of the
tasks in `extension_tasks`, or of every task when that is null.
Team.title: Team

Timeline.description:
A task's timeline in its contest, from its entry in `contest.yaml`,
each time at its default where the entry gives none: `worth`, the most
points it gives, 100 unless the entry says, and none on a task whose
latest publication gives no points or that has none; `release_at`, the
contest's start unless the entry says; `due`, after which a submission
is late, and `late_per_day`, the fraction a started late day takes off,
1 unless the entry says, both none on a task with no due; and `closes`,
the contest's end unless the entry says. `worth` and `late_per_day` are
exact.
Timeline.title: Timeline

TreeEntry.description:
One entry of a folder: a file, with the size of what its commit
holds, or a folder. `upload` tells an uploaded file from a typed one.
TreeEntry.title: TreeEntry

UpdateOrg.description: The org's description, and its display name when given.
UpdateOrg.title: UpdateOrg

Upload.description:
Where one upload stands: the input it is for, empty for a file an
organiser puts into the task, its name and content type, the size and
digest declared for it, and its status. `verified` is an upload a submit
or a save may name.
Upload.title: Upload

UploadInfo.description:
What a file that is an upload holds: the size and SHA-256 of the
bytes the forge's large-file store keeps for it. Its commit holds the
pointer to them, which is what `content` and `size` describe, so it is
never opened as text, and it is changed by uploading it again.
UploadInfo.title: UploadInfo

UploadRequest.description:
One file to upload for the task's contestant input `input`: where it
goes under the input, one name for a file input, a path of names for a
folder input, and `<group>/<test>` with or without an ending for an
input that takes one file per test; its size in bytes, the SHA-256 of
its content in lowercase hex and, when the browser knows it, its
content type.

The digest is what the forge checks the bytes against as they arrive, so
a file that changed between being read and being sent is refused there
rather than committed.
UploadRequest.title: UploadRequest

UploadStatus.description:
Where an upload stands: `waiting` until the forge holds its bytes,
`verified` once the forge says it does, and `consumed` once a commit
holds the pointer to it.

get.description:
The workflow `task.yaml` names as it is saved now, a draft included,
with each input it declares and each field every test has, in the
workflow's order. A workflow declares no defaults; a contestant input's
`default` is the task's own. A `task.yaml` that is missing or does not
read, names no workflow or one that cannot be read answers with
`problem`, the reason, and no inputs, so the form can mend it. Either
way `graded` says whether the task has a graded submission, from when
on a save refuses a test group it adds without its `show`, and `newer`
names the workflow's latest version when it comes after the one the
task names, which the task keeps until it is saved naming another.
